svg.title: Exploit chain behind Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935
svg.desc: Three steps from Volexity's October 13, 2026 report. Step one: a request to the public login script /dana-na/auth/url_default/welcome.cgi carries an X-DSCGI-PATH header naming a protected script; the URL decides access, the header decides the destination. Step two: the upload handler wu.cgi writes the file to disk before it checks that it is a valid ZIP, so the attacker runs the file in the window before it is deleted. Both steps are covered by CVE-2026-104935 and fixed in 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.5. Step three: the privileged dsinvoked service trusts DSCache data, which leads to a Perl script running as root. As of October 14, 2026 this step has no fix; Ivanti says one is due in the coming weeks.

A maintenance task is changed to run an attacker Perl script as root
No fix yet. Ivanti: "due in the coming weeks"
LDAP credential theft, LAPS and BitLocker key queries, renamed tcpdump, debug and audit logs edited
